title: Normalized ordinary supported Cartier Kummer map systems
statement: For a natural number $N$, use schemes [def-pc-scheme], the ordinary module derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], the concrete finite twist [lem-asd-finite-etale-twist-line], and the normalized supported boundary and divisor Chern class [def-asd-ordinary-supported-kummer-boundary]. Define a supported Kummer system to consist of a class $c_{D,A}\in\operatorname{Ext}^2_A(i_*A_D,A_T(1))$ for every finite commutative ring $A$ killed by $N$, every closed effective Cartier divisor $i:D\hookrightarrow T$, and every proof that $N$ is invertible on $T$. Require each class to satisfy the supported-boundary predicate. Specify a derived map $c_1:A_T\to A_T(1)[2]$ whose module-to-abelian realization is the concrete Kummer Chern class, and require the Ext realization of precomposition of $c_{D,A}$ with the constant inverse-image/direct-image unit $A_T\to i_*A_D$ to equal $c_1$. Under the canonical exact-direct-image comparison this is the same equation with the actual derived adjunction unit and source $Ri_*A_D$. The unit uses the derived adjunction [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] and the canonical constant comparison. The supported morphism is the Ext realization under the canonical single-object comparison for exact closed direct image [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-direct-image-exact]. Include a normalized roots-and-line inverse-image transport system [def-asd-ordinary-finite-p1-arrows]. For every cartesian square $D'\to D$, $T'\to T$ with both divisors effective Cartier, require the canonical constant-sheaf exchange to be invertible and require $c_{D',A}\circ\operatorname{Ex}=\operatorname{twist}\circ v^{-1}c_{D,A}$. For $N>0$ and every finite commutative coefficient ring $A$ killed by $N$, require the normalized derived scalar-extension relation from $\mathbf Z/N$ to $A$ [def-asd-ordinary-supported-kummer-scalar]. The class families and compatibility predicates are named interfaces for the fields. This defines the simultaneous datum and its canonical derived realization; it makes no assertion that such a datum exists.
